title: Maximin is Bounded by Minimax
body_html:
Maximin is Bounded by Minimax

For every finite matrix game,

$$\max_x \min_j E_A(x,j) \le \min_y \max_i E_A(i,y).$$

This is the weak-duality inequality: player I's best guaranteed payoff cannot exceed player II's best upper bound on player I's payoff.
proof_html:
For every mixed row $x$ and mixed column $y$, $$ \min_j E_A(x,j) \le E_A(x,y) \le \max_i E_A(i,y). $$ Taking the supremum over $x$ on the left preserves the first inequality against the fixed upper bound $\max_i E_A(i,y)$, so $$ \max_x \min_j E_A(x,j) \le \max_i E_A(i,y) $$ for every $y$. Taking the infimum over $y$ gives $$ \max_x \min_j E_A(x,j) \le \min_y \max_i E_A(i,y). $$

References

  • [MFoGT, Chapter 2, Lemmas 2.2.4 and 2.2.8] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. The lower value never exceeds the upper value.
